name: WAVM
workload: libsodium built-in benchmark suite (many crypto primitives plus codecs) compiled once to wasm32-wasi and run unchanged on each runtime; per-test execution time excluding initialization.
claimed_speedup: 'WAVM remains the fastest WebAssembly runtime, beating the competition in every single test'; 'about 15% faster than wasmer' (wasmer LLVM backend); V8 (Node.js) second. The page gives these as chart-backed statements, no per-test table in the README text.
tradeoffs: LLVM-based ahead-of-time compile, so slow compile and a large LLVM dependency; the author notes WAVM has no prebuilt aarch64 binaries and was skipped on ARM; the author recommends it for serverless use with memory snapshots.
caveats: Numbers are from builds dated 2021-02-21 (runtime versions of that day); every competitor has since changed by major versions. The same author's 2022-12 edition is in the repo (not read) and a June 2026 post (search snippet only, page not opened) reports a different ranking with Wasmer best and WAVM, WAMR and Wasmtime close, so treat WAVM's lead as dated. Hardware CPU model is not stated (tier B, not A). Evidence for a project already in the catalogue.

name: wasm3
workload: Same libsodium wasm32-wasi benchmark suite, interpreter-only comparison on macOS and on aarch64; per-test execution time excluding initialization.
claimed_speedup: 'wamr was slower than wasm3 on every single test'; native code is 'about 30 times faster' than wasm3 versus 'about 46 times faster' than WAMR (so wasm3 is roughly 1.5x faster than WAMR in aggregate, derived from page data); on aarch64 wasm3 runs at about 3% of native speed.
tradeoffs: Interpreter: about 30x slower than native here and far behind JIT/AOT runtimes; tiny footprint (README: about 64Kb code, about 10Kb RAM); README says wasm3 enters a minimal maintenance phase.
caveats: Builds from 2021-02-21; WAMR's fast interpreter was brand new then and has since changed. The page shows the 'about 30x' and 'about 46x' figures but the per-test chart is an image. CPU model not stated. Evidence for a project already in the catalogue.

name: Wasmtime
workload: Same libsodium wasm32-wasi benchmark suite; Cranelift-based runtimes compared on macOS x86_64 and on aarch64.
claimed_speedup: aarch64: 'wasmtime runs the test suite at ~54% the speed of native code' versus NodeJS 'around 49%'; 'Even with the same backend, wasmer is behind wasmtime, including on aarch64'; x86_64: wasmtime 'not far from LLVM-based runtimes' and ahead of Lucet (the slowest runtime in that run), which the author attributes to a new Cranelift backend.
tradeoffs: Cranelift favours fast compilation over peak code quality; in the same x86 run WAVM, an LLVM-based runtime, is the fastest overall.
caveats: Builds from 2021-02-21 (Cranelift new backend era); Wasmtime is not the fastest in this benchmark on x86 (WAVM and V8 lead), and the ARM claim rests on a single prepackaged wasmer binary whose other backends failed. A June 2026 post (search snippet only, not opened) says Wasmtime reaches 1.46x native with wide_arithmetic, unverified here. CPU model not stated. Evidence for a project already in the catalogue.
